<action type="say">
Here’s a script you can follow on the phone so it’s handled cleanly in one call. You can read it almost word for word.

---

**When you get through security and they ask how they can help:**

> I’m calling to dispute a duplicate charge on my credit card. It’s a Best Buy transaction for $249.99 on 2 November 2026 that’s been posted twice for the same purchase.

If they ask for card/transaction details, say:

> It’s on my main credit card, the one I use most often.  
> The merchant is Best Buy.  
> The amount is $249.99.  
> The date is 2 November 2026.  
> I see two separate posted entries for this same transaction, same date, same amount, same merchant.

**Describe the issue clearly:**

> I only made one purchase at Best Buy for $249.99 that day, but my card was charged twice.  
> I did not authorize a second transaction, and there was only one checkout and one receipt.  
> I’m requesting that you open a dispute and reverse the duplicate charge.

If they ask which of the two to dispute:

> Please dispute one of the two $249.99 Best Buy charges on 2 November 2026 — they’re duplicates of the same purchase, so either one is fine as long as one of them is reversed.

**If they ask follow-up questions (you can pre‑answer like this):**

- **Did you try to make two purchases?**  
  > No. I only made a single purchase. There was only one order and one receipt.

- **Was there any return or cancellation?**  
  > No, there was no return or cancellation. The issue is simply that the same charge appears twice.

- **Do you recognize the merchant and location?**  
  > Yes, I recognize Best Buy and the location. The problem is the duplicate billing for the same purchase.

If you have a receipt or email:

> I have a receipt/confirmation from Best Buy that shows only one purchase for $249.99 on that date, and I’m happy to provide it if you need supporting documentation.

**Ask them to confirm key points before you hang up:**

> Can you please confirm:  
> 1) That you’ve opened a dispute for the duplicate $249.99 Best Buy charge on 2 November 2026,  
> 2) The case or reference number, and  
> 3) When I should expect a temporary credit or final resolution?

Write down:
- **Case / dispute number**  
- **Which charge they flagged** (date/amount/merchant)  
- **Any timelines they mention** (e.g., “7–10 business days”)

---

If you tell me which bank or card issuer this is (e.g., Capital One, Chase, Amex, etc.), I can tighten this into a very short version tuned to their usual questions and even add what menu options to press to reach the right department.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s a NAB‑specific version you can use. You can keep this open and read it during the call.

---

### 1. Getting to the right team (NAB)

From Australia, you’ll usually call **13 22 65** (NAB general) or the number on the back of your card.

When the automated system answers, follow options like:
- “Credit cards”
- Then “Dispute a transaction” / “Something wrong with a transaction”
If there’s no clear option, just say **“operator”** or **“talk to a person”** and then tell the agent you need the **card disputes team**.

---

### 2. What to say to the NAB agent

**After they verify your identity and ask how they can help:**

> I’m calling to dispute a duplicate charge on my NAB credit card.  
> It’s a Best Buy transaction for $249.99 on 2 November 2026 that has been processed twice for the same purchase.

If they ask for details:

> The merchant is Best Buy.  
> The amount is $249.99.  
> The date is 2 November 2026.  
> I can see two separate posted charges for Best Buy for $249.99 on that date.  
> I only made one purchase and I only have one receipt.

**Clearly state what you want them to do:**

> I’d like you to raise a dispute and reverse the duplicate charge.  
> I authorised only one transaction. The second one is clearly a duplicate.

If they ask which one to dispute:

> Please dispute one of the two $249.99 Best Buy charges on 2 November 2026. They’re duplicates, so I just need one of them reversed.

---

### 3. Likely NAB questions and simple answers

- **“Do you recognise the merchant and location?”**  
  > Yes, I recognise Best Buy and the location. The issue isn’t the merchant, it’s that the same purchase has been billed twice.

- **“Did you make more than one purchase there that day?”**  
  > No, I only made one purchase. There was a single checkout and one receipt for $249.99.

- **“Have you spoken to the merchant?”**  
  > I haven’t been able to resolve it with the merchant / I’d prefer to raise this as a dispute through NAB because both charges have posted and it’s clearly a duplicate.

- **“Do you have proof of the original transaction?”**  
  > Yes, I have the Best Buy receipt or email confirmation showing only one purchase for $249.99 on that date, and I can provide it if needed.

---

### 4. Before you hang up, ask them to confirm:

> Can you please confirm:  
> 1) That you’ve lodged a dispute for the duplicate $249.99 Best Buy charge on 2 November 2026,  
> 2) The dispute or reference number, and  
> 3) Whether a temporary credit will be applied, and roughly how long the investigation will take?

Write down:
- Dispute / reference number  
- Date and time of the call  
- Any timeframes they give (for example, “up to 45 days”, “you’ll see a credit in X days”, etc.)

---

If you’d like, paste what you write down from the call here afterwards and I can help you interpret it or draft a follow‑up email/complaint if they don’t handle it properly.</action>
